tip: Regular comparatives add '-are': 'snabb' becomes 'snabbare' (faster).
'Betala' takes the bill directly, with no 'for': 'betalade räkningen' = paid the bill.
Being in a hurry uses 'ha' (have), not 'vara' (be): 'jag har bråttom'.
Adjectives ending in '-er' drop that 'e' before '-are': 'vacker' becomes 'vackrare' (more beautiful).
'Hålla med' (agree) is a two-part verb, and 'inte' goes between the parts: 'jag håller inte med'.
After 'kan' (can), the next verb takes no 'att' (to): 'det kan vara sant'.
'Det var inte meningen' is a set apology meaning 'I didn't mean to'.
'Flyta' (float) forms its past by changing the vowel, so it is 'flöt', not 'flytade': 'de flöt på vattnet'.
'Kliva av' means to get off a vehicle; 'av' (off) belongs to the verb: 'vi klev av bussen'.
With 'vi', the 'sig' of 'dra sig tillbaka' becomes 'oss': 'vi drog oss tillbaka' (we pulled back).
'Ha ont om' means to be short of something: 'jag har ont om tid' (short on time).
'Spela roll' means to matter, literally 'play a role': 'det spelar roll varje dag'.
'Klockan' plus a number = at that o'clock: 'klockan sju' = at seven.
'Tacka' pairs with 'för' to mark what you are grateful for: 'de tackar dig för hjälpen'.
'Sin'/'sitt'/'sina' all mean 'one's own'; 'sitt' is the 'ett'-word form: 'gav mig sitt telefonnummer'.
'Tänka' is to think in the sense of reckon or reflect: 'jag tänkte att det var du'.
The frame 'se' something 'som' means 'see as': 'jag ser det som en möjlighet'.
'Det går inte att' plus a verb means 'you can't' or 'there's no way to': 'det går inte att klaga'.
Swedish uses 'vill att' plus a full clause where English says 'want us to': 'vill att vi läser' (want us to read).
Start with an adverb and the verb still comes second, before the subject: 'självklart kommer jag'.
'Bestämma sig' = make up your mind; with 'vi' the 'sig' becomes 'oss': 'måste vi bestämma oss'.
'Längta' takes 'efter' for the thing you long for: 'jag längtar efter sommaren'.
'Sig' points back to the subject with 'han'/'hon'/'de': 'han delar med sig' = he shares.
Adjectives normally add '-a' in the plural: 'svenska köttbullar' = Swedish meatballs.
'Hävdade' (claimed/maintained) is formal; in everyday speech you'd usually just say 'sa' (said).
'Gråta' (cry) has an irregular past, 'grät': 'hon grät' = she cried.
'Som fan' roughly means 'as hell' and is vulgar; use it only in very casual speech.
'Sjunga' (sing) forms its past by changing the vowel, so it is 'sjöng', not 'sjungde': 'vi sjöng sånger'.
Short verbs like 'sy' take '-dde' in the past: 'sy' becomes 'sydde' = sewed.
'Fråga' takes the person directly, with no 'to': 'frågade oss' = asked us.
